text:
maria: Hey — following the quickstart on an M1 Mac after brew install, I hit a TLS error during `redwoodctl login --headless`.

samir: what error message?

maria: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` when the browser callback tries to reach the local callback URL. We're behind a corp proxy that injects a cert.

jen: Are HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars set? redwoodctl should respect those.

maria: HTTPS_PROXY is set. `curl https://localhost:12345` works with `--cacert /etc/ssl/corp-root.pem` but redwoodctl doesn't accept a CA path.

samir: redwoodctl uses Go tls which reads system roots, not arbitrary PEMs pointed at by env vars. There's an open ticket for `--cacert` but not shipped.

maria: Any quick workaround so new devs can finish the quickstart? The localtest server never sees the callback because the CLI fails the TLS handshake.

jen: You can add the corp CA to the macOS system keychain: `sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain /path/to/corp-root.pem`. Not ideal for onboarding.

maria: Adding to keychain fixes it. But we had users uncomfortable modifying keychains in the quickstart. This is a big DX friction.

samir: Agreed. This is a common failure mode: installer + corporate proxy + headless login. We should detect proxy-cert issues and surface guidance from `redwoodctl doctor` and the quickstart docs.

jen: Also the quickstart creates `~/.redwood/profiles/default` with `auth: headless` and `callback_url: http://localhost:12345`. When TLS fails the CLI retries quickly and spams auth logs. We should exponential backoff and show clearer errors.

maria: The repeated `login failed: tls: handshake error` messages are confusing and the token eventually times out. New devs get stuck.

samir: Two small fixes for short-term: 1) slow down retries (2 retries with backoff 2s -> 8s), 2) detect x509 unknown authority and print a helpful hint: "If you're on a corporate network with SSL inspection, add your corp CA to system trusts or run without the proxy."

jen: We can also detect common env vars like SSL_CERT_FILE and warn that redwoodctl doesn't read them.

samir: Good idea. Add a startup check that performs a TLS GET to the callback host; on cert failure capture the error and surface a doc link.

maria: Another thing: Homebrew's postinstall message only says `run redwoodctl init`. Our sample app expects a `quickstart` profile. New users get `default` and then env conflicts.

jen: Update installer message: "run `redwoodctl init --profile quickstart` to set up the sample app". Also make `redwoodctl init` interactive and print a one-line summary of created files.

ci-bot: deploy-check: lint passed on doc patch branch `devex/quickstart-proxy-help`

maria: Final oddity: localtest binds to 127.0.0.1 by default; if someone is using Docker with host networking the callback might be reachable but cert mismatch occurs because the proxy cert is for an internal host. Maybe we need `--insecure-local-callback`?

samir: I'd avoid an "insecure" flag. Prefer `--local-callback-host` to override the host:port and `--trust-local-ca /path/to/ca.pem` for headless flows. Document `--trust-local-ca` as dev-only and do NOT persist it to system trust stores.

jen: `--trust-local-ca` seems like a reasonable compromise. Keep it scoped to the headless login session. Also make the doctor command explain how to use it.

maria: I'll open a ticket capturing the TLS stack traces and propose the doctor + installer doc patches.

samir: Assign to devex, tag `redwoodctl`, cc eng-infra and eng-ml (they hit the same for model downloads).

maria: Filing now. I'll include a small patch for the retry/backoff and a doc change for the quickstart.

jen: thanks! :raised_hands:
